title: Publish portable Studio workspace packages
summary: A Studio Board, linked imported truth, component instances, overrides, proposals, evidence, and unresolved conflicts can travel as one versioned package with stable identity and revision lineage instead of remaining machine-local editor state.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned `studio_workspace` payload is defined as an explicit repository-owned schema and is carried inside the shared Humble Artifact Envelope rather than an untyped metadata dictionary.

The envelope uses a repository-qualified artifact ID, artifact kind, schema version, producer repository, producer revision, created/observed timestamps, content hash, visibility, sensitivity, freshness, and source evidence references.
The repository remains the semantic source of truth for the payload; HumbleControl may index and route the artifact but cannot reinterpret or overwrite domain fields.
The workspace package distinguishes imported source snapshots, user-authored board state, derived previews, pending proposals, accepted proposals, and external implementation receipts.
Linked repository artifacts retain qualified IDs, pinned revisions, last-known snapshots, and stale/missing/conflict states.
Board assets use integrity metadata and relative package paths; bookmarks, credentials, absolute paths, and private source are never embedded.
Opening offline is supported from the package snapshot and never silently refreshes linked repositories.

Serialization is deterministic for unchanged semantic state, round-trips without data loss, and has fixtures for valid, missing, corrupt, unsupported-version, unknown-extension, and intentionally redacted payloads.
Publication is idempotent: republishing the same qualified artifact revision produces no duplicate, while changed content requires a new revision or explicit supersession link.
Offline opening uses the artifact snapshot and reports unavailable live sources without silently refreshing or changing the stored content.
Visibility and sensitivity are field-aware; secrets, credentials, raw local absolute paths, unrelated personal data, and unapproved private evidence are excluded by default.
Schema migration and compatibility behavior are documented, testable, and conservative; unsupported data fails with an actionable state rather than partial silent decoding.
The producer passes the shared conformance fixtures from `mrPoky/HumbleControl#HC-0165` plus its repository-native tests, build, contract, and diff gates with zero app-owned warnings.
The completed ticket records one generated example artifact, validation output, artifact hash, producer revision, and a human-readable explanation of what downstream consumers may and may not assume.

agent_notes: Portfolio Convergence Wave 3; repository-owned artifact producer ticket.
Estimated effort: L-XL, approximately 5-10 focused working days after prerequisites.
Implementation risk: high because identity, compatibility, privacy, and downstream assumptions become durable contracts.

User outcome: A Studio Board, linked imported truth, component instances, overrides, proposals, evidence, and unresolved conflicts can travel as one versioned package with stable identity and revision lineage instead of remaining machine-local editor state.
External portfolio prerequisites: mrPoky/HumbleControl#HC-0161, mrPoky/HumbleControl#HC-0162, mrPoky/HumbleControl#HC-0165.
Non-scope: do not centralize domain truth in HumbleControl, add cloud synchronization, expose secrets or private history, or introduce direct cross-repository writes.
Alternative considered and rejected: exchange ad hoc JSON or deep links without a shared envelope — this cannot preserve revision, provenance, visibility, consent, compatibility, or idempotency.
Do not claim live interoperability until producer conformance, consumer conformance, one end-to-end fixture, and repository-native verification have passed.

Wave 8 portfolio reassessment: retain-conditional; priority band later. Optional platform interoperability remains useful, but independent product quality now takes precedence and no merger is implied.
Wave 10 final rationalization: consolidate-into-fusion-program; portfolio band later. Keep only as input to the reversible platform fusion program.
Wave 11 execution reconciliation: `optional-reference-or-research`. Use the Wave 11 implementation program as the delivery entry point while preserving this ticket's evidence and intent.

Wave 12 deep reassessment: decision `retain-optional`, relevance `later`, current priority `medium`, execution gate `proven product need and explicit consented boundary`. Cross-application work remains conditional and must not displace standalone product quality or the game completion gates.
Wave 13 human-validation reassessment: `retain-platform-reference` / `later` / priority `medium`. Cross-app work is valid only when a validated user or operator need exists.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid-research-or-reference`; publication `publish-as-proposed-backlog`; implementation sequence `later`. Cross-app work is valid only when a validated user or operator need exists.
